key_insight: The quadratic compute/memory bottleneck in offline feed‑forward multi‑view 3D reconstruction comes from a variable‑length Key‑Value (KV) scene representation; distilling that KV space into a fixed‑size MLP via test‑time training preserves geometry while removing the quadratic scaling.
problem_solved: Offline feed‑forward 3D reconstruction methods scale poorly: compute and memory grow roughly quadratically with the number of input images because the KV scene representation length varies with views.
method: Encode multi‑view inputs into a variable‑length Key‑Value (KV) geometry representation as in prior feed‑forward systems.
Perform test‑time training to distill the variable KV set into a fixed‑size MLP that implicitly represents scene geometry.
Use the compact MLP for downstream feed‑forward reconstruction, reducing memory and compute growth from quadratic to constant per‑scene representation (and linear overall with views).
impact: Enables scalable, high‑quality offline feed‑forward 3D reconstruction on large image collections by cutting memory/computation costs and simplifying deployment; useful for practitioners working with multi‑view datasets or large scene batches.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: many input images → KV encoder → test‑time distillation → fixed‑size MLP → reconstructed 3D output

paper_title: VGG-T$^3$: Offline Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction at Scale
paper_authors: Sven Elflein, Ruilong Li, Sérgio Agostinho, Zan Gojcic, Laura Leal-Taixé
